13: # Web Layout and Sizing
14: 
15: The CSS layout mechanics behind stacking, sizing, containers and scrolling.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: This file covers stacking contexts, containing blocks, intrinsic sizing, grid tracks, containers and scrolling behavior.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Changing how a fixed, sticky or stacked element is positioned.
28: - Sizing flex or grid tracks, or a container query, around intrinsic content.
29: - Handling media ratio, scrollbar space, scroll chaining or viewport height units.
30: - Adding a content-sized control or an intrinsic-size animation.
31: 
32: ### Boundaries
33: 
34: - **Baseline flow and responsive rules.** The baseline flow and responsive rules remain in [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. STACKING AND CONTAINING BLOCKS
39: 
40: ### L1. Ancestors that capture fixed positioning
41: 
42: - **Rule:** Keep transforms, filters, perspective, paint or layout containment, relevant `will-change` values and `container-type` off ancestors of viewport-fixed headers or bars.
43: - **Why:** These properties can make an ancestor the containing block for a fixed descendant, so the descendant moves with that ancestor instead of the viewport. Transform, filter and containment behavior is longstanding.
44: - **When not to:** Scope a fixed child to an ancestor only when it is meant to remain fixed inside that component.
45: - **Pitfall:** Adding `will-change: transform` to smooth an ancestor can silently change where a fixed child is positioned.
46: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-08-14 (web-features `container-queries`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 110 / Safari 16.
47: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Containing_block)
48: 
49: ### L2. Stacking context triggers
50: 
51: - **Rule:** Inspect the ancestor chain for a stacking context before increasing a `z-index` value.
52: - **Why:** A stacking context is painted as one unit, so a descendant cannot out-rank content in a different context. Triggers include the root, positioned elements with non-auto `z-index`, fixed or sticky positioning, flex or grid items with `z-index`, opacity below one, blend modes, `transform`, `translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, filters, perspective, clipping, masks, `isolation: isolate`, `contain: layout`, `contain: paint`, `contain: strict`, `contain: content`, `container-type`, `content-visibility: auto` and `will-change` naming one of these properties. Top-layer elements paint above ordinary stacking contexts.
53: - **When not to:** Raise a local `z-index` when the elements already share the same stacking context and the order alone is wrong.
54: - **Pitfall:** An opacity such as `0.999` creates a stacking context, while `isolation: isolate` creates one without changing opacity or clipping paint.
55: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
56: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS stacking context](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_positioned_layout/Stacking_context)
57: 
58: ### L3. Flow root without clipping
59: 
60: - **Rule:** Use `display: flow-root` to contain floats or stop margin collapse when clipping is not required.
61: - **Why:** A flow root establishes a block formatting context without turning overflow into a clipping or scrolling rule.
62: - **When not to:** Use an overflow value when clipping is an intentional part of the component.
63: - **Pitfall:** `overflow: hidden` can clip content and prevent sticky descendants from sticking to their scrollport.
64: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
65: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS block formatting context](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_display/Block_formatting_context)
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. INTRINSIC AND GRID SIZING
70: 
71: ### L4. Automatic minimum on flex and grid items
72: 
73: - **Rule:** Set `min-width: 0` or `min-inline-size: 0` on a flex or grid child that must shrink below its min-content size.
74: - **Why:** The automatic minimum can preserve the longest unbreakable content width, so the item refuses to shrink to the available track.
75: - **When not to:** Keep the automatic minimum when the item's content must set a lower bound on its track.
76: - **Pitfall:** Setting `overflow: hidden` may hide the overflow while leaving the sizing constraint in place.
77: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
78: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS min-width](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/min-width)
79: 
80: ### L5. Grid tracks, subgrid and auto repetition
81: 
82: - **Rule:** Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` when long content must not widen a flexible track, use subgrid when nested items must share parent tracks, and choose `auto-fit` or `auto-fill` by whether empty tracks should collapse.
83: - **Why:** A bare `1fr` has an automatic minimum. Subgrid reuses the parent grid tracks. `auto-fit` collapses empty repeated tracks, while `auto-fill` preserves them.
84: - **When not to:** Keep the intrinsic minimum when content must determine the track size, or use independent tracks when nested columns should not align with the parent.
85: - **Pitfall:** One unbreakable string can widen a grid whose flexible track still has an automatic minimum.
86: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
87: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS subgrid](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout/Subgrid)
88: 
89: ### L6. Container queries and container units
90: 
91: - **Rule:** Put query containment on a wrapper and query from its descendants, then use container units such as `cqi` or `cqw` where sizing should follow that wrapper.
92: - **Why:** A query container cannot use its own size query to style itself. `container-type: inline-size` also establishes containment that can affect fixed descendants and stacking.
93: - **When not to:** Use a viewport media query when the layout decision depends on the viewport rather than the component's available size.
94: - **Pitfall:** Adding `container-type` to the styled component itself does not make that component respond to its own size.
95: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-08-14 (web-features `container-queries`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 110 / Safari 16.
96: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS container size and style queries](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_containment/Container_size_and_style_queries)
97: 
98: ---
99: 
100: ## 4. MEDIA AND SCROLL GEOMETRY
101: 
102: ### L7. Intrinsic media ratio
103: 
104: - **Rule:** Keep an image's or video's intrinsic `width` and `height` attributes consistent with its CSS `aspect-ratio`.
105: - **Why:** The attributes give the browser a ratio before media loads, while CSS controls the rendered box after styles apply.
106: - **When not to:** Let intrinsic ratio determine the box when the media is not constrained by a fixed layout slot.
107: - **Pitfall:** A conflicting CSS ratio can reserve one shape before load and display another after load.
108: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-03-20 (web-features `aspect-ratio`). Chrome 88 / Firefox 89 / Safari 15.
109: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS aspect-ratio](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/aspect-ratio)
110: 
111: ### L8. Stable scrollbar space
112: 
113: - **Rule:** Apply `scrollbar-gutter: stable` to the element that owns scrolling when content changes would shift its inline layout.
114: - **Why:** The stable gutter reserves space for a classic scrollbar before overflow appears.
115: - **When not to:** Skip it when the platform uses overlay scrollbars and reserving space would add unwanted width.
116: - **Pitfall:** `stable both-edges` reserves space on both sides and can make a narrow pane needlessly smaller. Without a stable gutter, a classic scrollbar can shift the inline layout.
117: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-12-11 (web-features `scrollbar-gutter`). Chrome 94 / Firefox 97 / Safari 18.2.
118: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS scrollbar-gutter](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/scrollbar-gutter)
119: 
120: ### L9. Scroll chaining and snap points
121: 
122: - **Rule:** Use `overscroll-behavior: contain` on an inner pane that must stop scroll chaining, and use scroll snap only when a destination should settle at defined positions.
123: - **Why:** The contain value keeps overscroll from propagating to an ancestor. Scroll snap adjusts the final scroll position toward configured snap areas.
124: - **When not to:** Keep normal chaining when users should continue scrolling the page after reaching the end of a pane.
125: - **Pitfall:** The `chain` value is unavailable in some browsers. Feature-detect it and keep the default or `contain` path.
126: - **Support:** Baseline limited availability (web-features `overscroll-behavior`). Chrome 144 / Firefox 150 / Safari unsupported. Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `scroll-snap`). Chrome 69 / Firefox 68 / Safari 11.
127: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS overscroll-behavior](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overscroll-behavior)
128: 
129: ### L10. Small, large and dynamic viewport heights
130: 
131: - **Rule:** Choose `svh` for the small visible viewport, `lvh` for the largest viewport and `dvh` when the layout should track browser chrome changes.
132: - **Why:** Mobile browser controls make the visible viewport change. The legacy `vh` behavior corresponds to the large viewport and can extend behind visible browser chrome.
133: - **When not to:** Use a content-driven height when the section should grow with its contents rather than fill a viewport.
134: - **Pitfall:** A `dvh` panel can resize while scrolling, while `lvh` can extend beyond the currently visible area.
135: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
136: - **See also:** [MDN: Viewport-percentage length units](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/length#relative_length_units_based_on_viewport)
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: ## 5. INTRINSIC SIZE ENHANCEMENTS
141: 
142: ### L11. Content-sized controls and intrinsic-size animation
143: 
144: - **Rule:** Feature-detect `field-sizing: content` as an enhancement, and feature-detect `interpolate-size` or `calc-size()` as optional animation enhancements.
145: - **Why:** `field-sizing` lets supported controls size from their content. Intrinsic-size interpolation extends animation beyond numeric lengths and remains unavailable in several browsers.
146: - **When not to:** Use a stable row count when a control must keep a fixed editing area, or omit the animation when an instant state change is clear.
147: - **Pitfall:** Shipping either feature as the only layout or interaction path leaves browsers without it with a fixed default size or no transition.
148: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2026-06-16 (web-features `field-sizing`). Chrome 123 / Firefox 152 / Safari 26.2. Baseline limited availability (web-features `interpolate-size`). Chrome 129 / Firefox unsupported / Safari unsupported. Baseline limited availability (web-features `calc-size`). Chrome 129 / Firefox unsupported / Safari unsupported.
149: - **See also:** [MDN: CSS field-sizing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/field-sizing)
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ## 6. LOGICAL PROPERTIES
154: 
155: For right-to-left direction and writing-mode mapping, follow [I4 in web-internationalization.md](web-internationalization.md#i4-logical-properties-and-writing-modes).
156: 
157: ---
158:

164: |---|---:|---:|---:|---|

169: | `overscroll-behavior: chain` | 144 | 150 | unsupported | limited availability (web-features `overscroll-behavior`) |
170: | Scroll snap | 69 | 68 | 11 | widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `scroll-snap`) |
171: | `field-sizing` | 123 | 152 | 26.2 | newly available since 2026-06-16 (web-features `field-sizing`) |

53: 
54: - **Rule:** Set `dir="rtl"` for a right-to-left document and use `dir="auto"` for user-provided strings with unknown direction.

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
330: 
331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```
335: 
336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead
340: 
341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
344: 
345: **Format**:
346: ```markdown
347: ### [Pattern Name]
348: 
349: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]
350: \```[language]
351: // Bad code with issues
352: // Showing what NOT to do
353: \```
354: 
355: **AFTER**: [Solution description]
356: \```[language]
357: // Good code with fixes
358: // Showing correct approach
359: \```
360: 
361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale
369: 
370: ### Pattern Comparison Tables
371: 
372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
373: 
374: **Format**:
375: ```markdown
376: ### Common Patterns
377: 
378: | Scenario     | Approach A (Wrong) | Approach B (Right) | Why Better  |
379: | ------------ | ------------------ | ------------------ | ----------- |
380: | [Scenario 1] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
382: ```
383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison
385: 
386: ### Decision Logic in Markdown
387: 
388: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions
389: 
390: **Format**:
391: \```markdown
392: ### Decision Logic
393: 
394: \```markdown
395: IF [condition A]:
396:   → [Action/Path A]
397:   → [Expected outcome A]
398: 
399: IF [condition B]:
400:   → [Action/Path B]
401:   → [Expected outcome B]
402: 
403: IF [condition C]:
404:   → [Action/Path C]
405:   → [Expected outcome C]
406: \```
407: \```
408: 
409: **Alternative format** (decision tree):
410: \```markdown
411: \```
412: Analyze situation
413: ├─ Condition A met
414: │  └─ Execute Workflow A
415: │     └─ Expected outcome A
416: ├─ Condition B met
417: │  └─ Execute Workflow B
418: │     └─ Expected outcome B
419: └─ Condition C met
420:    └─ Execute Workflow C
421:       └─ Expected outcome C
422: \```
423: \```
424: 
425: ### Validation Checkpoints
426: 
427: **Purpose**: Named checkpoints throughout workflows
428: 
429: **Format**:
430: ```markdown
431: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
432: ```
433: 
434: **Examples**:
435: - `files_analyzed`
436: - `artifacts_filtered`
437: - `strategy_determined`
438: - `root_cause_identified`
439: 
440: **Usage**: Reference in quality checklists and debugging
441: 
442: ### Prerequisites Section
443: 
444: **Purpose**: Link to required standards and context
445: 
446: > **PLACEMENT**: Prerequisites go in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph.
447: 
448: **Format**:
449: ```markdown
450: # [Workflow Name]
451: 
452: [1-2 sentence summary only - no prerequisites here]
453: 
454: ---
455: 
456: \## 1. OVERVIEW
457: 
458: ### Prerequisites
459: Follow [standard name] for all implementations:
460: - **[Standard 1]**: [Brief description]
461: - **[Standard 2]**: [Brief description]
462: - See [standard-file.md](./standard-file.md) for complete requirements
463: ```
464: 
465: **Key Elements**:
466: - Appears in Section 1 OVERVIEW, not intro
467: - Links to other reference files
468: - Lists specific requirements
469: 
470: ### Tool Integration References
471: 
472: **Purpose**: Show MCP tool usage, script execution, asset references
473: 
474: **Format for MCP Tools**:
475: \```markdown
476: **Automated [Task] via MCP:**
477: 
478: Instead of [manual approach], use Chrome DevTools MCP:
479: 
480: \```markdown
481: 1. [Step 1]:
482:    [Use tool: mcp__chrome_devtools__tool_name]
483:    - parameter1: "value"
484:    - parameter2: value
485: 
486: 2. [Step 2]:
487:    [Use tool: mcp__chrome_devtools__tool_name]
488: \```
489: 
490: **What you'll see:**
491: - [Expected output 1]
492: - [Expected output 2]
493: 
494: **Example output:**
495: \```json
496: {
497:   "field": "value",
498:   "data": "example"
499: }
500: \```
501: \```
502: 
503: **Format for Scripts**:
504: ```markdown
505: **See also:** [script_name.js](../scripts/script_name.js) for production-ready implementation
506: ```
507: 
508: **Format for Assets**:
509: ```markdown
510: **See also:** [template-name.md](../assets/template-name.md) for complete templates
511: ```
512: 
513: ### Common Error Patterns
514: 
515: **Purpose**: Document actual errors with explanations
516: 
517: **Format**:
518: \```markdown
519: **Common [System/Browser] Errors:**
520: 
521: \```javascript
522: // [Actual error message]
523: // → [What it means]
524: // → [How to fix]
525: 
526: // [Another error message]
527: // → [What it means]
528: // → [How to fix]
529: \```
530: \```
531: 
532: **Example**:
533: \```markdown
534: **Common Browser Errors:**
535: 
536: \```javascript
537: // Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'X' of undefined
538: // → Variable is undefined, check initialization
539: // → Verify element exists before accessing properties
540: 
541: // Failed to load resource: net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT
542: // → Ad blocker or browser extension blocking resource
543: // → Check Network tab, test with extensions disabled
544: \```
545: \```
546: 
547: ### Scope Limitations
548: 
549: **Purpose**: Explicitly state what's in/out of scope
550: 
551: **Format**:
552: ```markdown
553: **Note:** [Clarification of what IS supported]
554: 
555: **Out of scope:** [What is NOT supported]
556: ```
557: 
558: **Example**:
559: ```markdown
560: **Note:** All browser testing done via Chrome DevTools MCP.
561: 
562: **Out of scope:** Cross-browser testing in Firefox, Safari (MCP is Chrome-only)
563: ```

565: ### Browser Testing Checklists
566: 
567: **Purpose**: Specific viewport tests with checkboxes
568: 
569: **Format**:
570: \```markdown

572: 
573: \```markdown

575: □ Mobile viewport (375px) - use DevTools emulation

578: □ Test viewport transitions (320px, 768px, 1920px)
579: \```
580: \```

584: ### Phased Workflow with Checkpoints Example
585: 
586: **Purpose**: Show complete workflow with validation gates
587: 
588: **Format**:
589: ```yaml

680: ---
681: 
682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073:

=== OLD i18n I4
## 2. LAYOUT AND DIRECTIONAL ICONS

### I4. Logical properties and writing modes

**Rule.** Use the CSS mapping in [web-layout-and-sizing.md](web-layout-and-sizing.md#5-logical-properties) when dimensions and edges must follow the writing mode.
**Why.** The layout reference owns the physical-to-logical property mechanics and their interaction with writing modes.
**When not to.** Keep physical coordinates for intentionally physical surfaces such as a canvas whose origin is fixed to the left edge.
**Pitfall.** Mixing physical and logical sides in one rule lets declaration order choose the edge in one direction and a different edge in another.
**Support.** Judgment, no version gate.
**See also.** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_logical_properties_and_values

### I5. Directional icon mirroring

**Rule.** Mirror arrows and chevrons whose meaning follows inline reading direction, and keep direction-neutral or physical icons unchanged.
**Why.** Directional icons encode forward or backward movement, while a logo, clock, checkmark or media control keeps the same meaning in either writing direction.
**When not to.** Do not mirror an icon whose symbol depicts a fixed physical object or an invariant action.
**Pitfall.** Mirroring a play or checkmark icon reverses a symbol whose meaning does not depend on text direction.
**Support.** Judgment, no version gate.
**See also.** https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-scripts

23: This file covers widget behavior, focus and browser accessibility preferences. Support summaries use the web-features Baseline classifications and browser-version data.

26: 
27: - Adding or changing a modal dialog

41: ## 2. MODAL DIALOG CONTRACT
42: 
43: ### A1. Modal dialog
44: 
45: - **Rule:** Use native `<dialog>` with `showModal()` or a component library's documented modal behavior.
46: - **Why:** These mechanisms provide top-layer placement, Escape handling, focus containment and an inert background.
47: - **When not to:** Use a non-modal dialog when the surrounding page must remain interactive.
48: - **Pitfall:** Setting `aria-modal="true"` on an ordinary element hides the rest of the page from assistive technology without making the page inert.
49: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `dialog`). Chrome 37 / Firefox 98 / Safari 15.4.
50: - **See also:** [WAI-ARIA APG: Dialog (modal)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 3. LIBRARY MAPPING
55: 
56: | Pattern | Integration boundary |
57: |---|---|
58: | Modal dialog | Close through the dialog lifecycle so focus returns to the opener. |
59: | Menu button | Use a disclosure and navigation list for site navigation; a menu role promises menu keyboard behavior. |
60: | Tabs, listbox or combobox | Do not add tabindex values or arrow-key handlers when a component manages roving focus; treat its autocomplete as a combobox and do not redeclare supplied roles. |
61: | Accordion, disclosure or tooltip | Keep expanded state aligned; disabled controls may not receive focus, and a tooltip cannot be the only label. |
62: | Status region, table or grid | Keep the live region mounted before changing its text; set `aria-sort` on the sorted header when needed. |
63: | Focus styling | Keep a visible replacement if an outline is removed. |
64: 
65: When a component library provides widget roles, state, focus movement or announcements, use that behavior as the source of truth. For hand-written widgets, implement the complete pattern described below.

### Boundaries

This file does not own:

- **Web mechanics.** The web layer expresses the principles through DOM and CSS. It names the vocabulary and mechanics that implement them, in [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
- **Project-specific conventions.** Each project mode adds the conventions it uses, in its own `SKILL.md`.

---

## 2. THE ELEVEN PRINCIPLES

1. **Actions are buttons, and navigation is links.** People get the expected interaction and navigation behavior. See [web structure](web-markup-and-css.md#2-structure-and-semantics).
2. **Every control has a name, a role and a state.** People need to identify a control and understand its current condition. See [web structure](web-markup-and-css.md#2-structure-and-semantics).
3. **Every input has a visible label, and its affordance matches the data.** A visible label stays available after a person starts typing, while the input cue helps them enter the right data. See [web forms](web-markup-and-css.md#3-forms).
4. **Layout follows content flow, siblings have consistent spacing, text containers grow with their text, overlays leave the flow, and content respects device safe areas.** This lets content adapt without clipping or hiding ordinary content. See [web layout](web-markup-and-css.md#4-layout).
5. **Text survives translation and font scaling.** Longer translations and larger system text must remain readable and reachable. See [web responsive rules](web-markup-and-css.md#5-responsive).
6. **Every image has a text-alternative decision and reserved dimensions.** People using assistive technology need the image's meaning, and the layout needs its space before it loads. See [web media](web-markup-and-css.md#6-media).
7. **Values come from installed tokens, and a missing token is reported.** Installed tokens keep values consistent across the app, while a report gives the design system a clear gap to resolve. See [web CSS architecture](web-markup-and-css.md#7-css-architecture).
8. **Figma is a reference, not a code structure.** A design shows intended appearance and states, while the app's own conventions decide its structure. See the [web boundary](web-markup-and-css.md#1-overview) and [Figma to code](figma-to-code.md).
9. **Responsive behavior is checked at narrow, medium and wide widths and under zoom.** These checks expose wrapping, overflow and clipping before release. See [web responsive rules](web-markup-and-css.md#5-responsive).
10. **Assistive-technology checks are part of completion, and non-essential motion respects the user's reduced-motion setting.** They confirm names, order, states and feedback when people do not use the visual layout. See the [web checklist](web-markup-and-css.md#9-pre-completion-checklist).
11. **Text and controls meet the contrast target set by sk-design-fundamentals on every theme the mode supports.** Contrast remains readable in each supported theme. See [web structure](web-markup-and-css.md#2-structure-and-semantics) and [sk-design-fundamentals](../../../sk-design/sk-design-fundamentals/SKILL.md).

---

## 3. VALUES AND PRECEDENCE

=== figma cite
| Icon instance | The app's icon component, or inline SVG with `currentColor` |

A row with no token to map to is a finding to report, not a reason to paste the Figma value.

---

## 4. WORKFLOW

1. Read the design context with a read-only Figma transport from the Section 5 tool ladder.

state.output: ### L2. Stacking context triggers - **Rule:** Inspect the ancestor chain for a stacking context before increasing a `z-index` value. - **Why:** A stacking context is painted as one unit, so a descendant cannot out-rank content in a different context. Triggers include the root, positioned elements with non-auto `z-index`, fixed or sticky positioning, flex or grid items with `z-index`, opacity below one, blend modes, `transform`, `translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, filters, perspective, clipping, masks, `isolation: isolate`, `contain: layout`, `contain: paint`, `contain: strict`, `contain: content`, `container-type`, `content-visibility: auto` and `will-change` naming one of these properties. Baseline limited availability (web-features `calc-size`). Chrome 38 / Firefox 38 / Safari 10.1. - **See also:** [MDN: Responsive images](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Guides/Responsive_images) ### P9. Picture formats and image hints - **Rule:** List preferred AVIF and WebP sources before the JPEG `` fallback, use loading, decoding and priority hints for their intended stages, and use `sizes="auto"` only as an enhancement. - **Why:** The browser selects the first supported `` in a ``. `fetchpriority` guides scheduling, `loading` changes fetch timing, `decoding` guides display scheduling and explicit `sizes` values remain the baseline when `sizes="auto"` is unavailable. - **When not to:** Use one `` when there is no format, density or art-direction choice. - **Pitfall:** Lazy-loading the LCP image fights its need to load early. Follow the [LCP rule](#p1-largest-contentful-paint-resource). - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-10-29 (web-features `fetch-priority`). Chrome 103 / Firefox 132 / Safari 17.2. Baseline widely available since 2026-06-19 (web-features `loading-lazy`). Chrome 77 / Firefox 121 / Safari 16.4. Baseline: no web-features entry. Chrome 65 / Firefox 63 / Safari 11.1. Baseline limited availability (web-features `sizes-auto`). Chrome 126 / Firefox 150 / Safari unsupported. - **See also:** [MDN: HTML picture element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/picture) === perf 104-121 - **Rule:** Add `will-change` shortly before the property starts animating and remove it when the animation ends. - **Why:** The hint can prompt early rendering preparation, but it can also create a stacking context, containing block or extra graphics memory use. - **When not to:** Do not add the hint when a measured animation does not benefit from preparation. - **Pitfall:** Leaving `will-change: transform` on a permanent page shell can change fixed descendants and retain an unnecessary rendering layer. - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `will-change`). Chrome 36 / Firefox 36 / Safari 9.1. - **See also:** [MDN: CSS will-change](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/will-change) ### P10. Main-thread long tasks - **Rule:** Split, move or yield work that blocks the main thread for more than 50 milliseconds. - **Why:** A long task delays input and rendering until the browser can run another task. - **When not to:** Keep a bounded task together when it completes below the long-task threshold and does not delay an interaction. - **Pitfall:** A third-party script can block input even when the app's own handlers are short. - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate. - **See also:** [web.dev: Optimize long tasks](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-long-tasks) ---
